routes.status_note: CJEU Grand Chamber judgment in Commission v Malta, Case C-181/23 (2025-04-29) held the transactional investor-citizenship scheme in breach of Art. 20 TFEU and Art. 4(3) TEU. Act XXI of 2025 rewrote Cap. 188 Art. 10(9) as grant 'by merit'; LN 159 of 2025 deleted the MEIN investment requirements, fee schedules and caps. MEIN applications not approved before 2025-04-29 ceased to have effect; citizenship already granted remains valid. Community Malta Agency (2026-02-05): Citizenship by Merit is 'neither a programme nor a scheme, pathway, continuation, or alternative' to the repealed framework — it must never be marketed as an investment route.

Counting windows (art. 15(3)): residence is counted within a maximum span of 9 years (CPLP/EU), 12 years (others) or 6 years (stateless). Transitional rule (art. 7(2)): procedures PENDING at entry into force are assessed under the previous law - the old 5-year term survives only for those. Also required (art. 6(1)): sufficient knowledge of the Portuguese language AND of Portuguese culture, history and national symbols (by test or certificate - the statute sets no CEFR level; levels sit in the Nationality Regulation, under revision), knowledge of fundamental rights and duties and of the political organisation of the Portuguese state, a solemn declaration of adherence to the democratic principles of the rule of law, and demonstrated capacity for subsistence. routes.time_to_pr: The golden visa is itself the longest residence form; there is no investment-based permanent-residence or naturalisation track (citizenship only by exceptional federal decree)
routes.dual_citizenship: Not recognised as a general rule - renunciation is required: Constitution art. 8 (nationality is single, as specified by law); Nationality Law No. 17 of 1972 art. 11 ('No one may be naturalised without renouncing the nationality of origin') and art. 12-Bis(1); art. 15(c) provides deprivation on voluntary foreign naturalisation. Exception (2021, per u.ae): executive-regulation amendments allow specific NOMINATED categories - investors, doctors, specialists, inventors, scientists, intellectuals and creative talents/artists - and their spouses and children to acquire Emirati nationality while retaining their original nationality; grants run only through nomination by the Rulers'/Crown Princes' Courts, Executive Council offices or the Cabinet, and holders must report acquiring or losing any other citizenship.

Land-department title/valuation proof for real estate

routes.programme: Malta Permanent Residence Programme (MPRP, Residency Malta Agency)
routes.status_note: Third-country nationals only (non-EU/EEA/Swiss). Fee structure rebuilt by Legal Notice 146 of 2025 (unified contribution, higher admin fee, no per-person fees for spouse/minor children, temporary residence available during processing); property thresholds were reset by LN 310 of 2024 from 2025-01-01. The LN 146 gazette effective date was not read this round (professional sources differ) — amounts below are the Agency's current published figures, which settle.

routes.gov_fees: Non-refundable admin fee 60,000; government contribution 37,000 (purchase and rental unified); 7,500 per adult dependant excluding the spouse; NGO donation 2,000; residence card 500/person (5 years). Assets test: capital assets >= 500,000 (of which >= 150,000 financial) or >= 650,000 (of which >= 75,000 financial). Applications only via a Licensed Agent.

routes.residence_requirement: Residence certificate is indefinite while programme obligations are met; card renewed every 5 years. No minimum-stay figure is set on the Agency pages read (an explicit 'no minimum stay' sentence was not re-read — partial).
routes.time_to_pr: The MPRP is itself permanent residence (the Agency states it is distinct from citizenship law)
routes.time_to_citizenship: No investment-citizenship route (abolished, see malta-cbi); naturalisation is discretionary after long actual residence
routes.dual_citizenship: Allowed: Maltese Citizenship Act (Cap. 188, as amended by Act IV of 2000) - renunciation (art. 13) is a voluntary declaration by a citizen who also holds a foreign nationality, and the deprivation grounds (art. 14) do not include acquiring or holding another nationality. Dual citizenship recognised since 2000; no MPRP rule requires renouncing a previous nationality.
routes.restricted_nationalities: EU/EEA/Swiss nationals are ineligible (third-country programme); sanctioned-country nationals excluded per Agency rules
documents: Health insurance covering Malta and Europe
Proof of stable income and of the assets test

routes.gov_fees: Application fee EUR 500 per application (criteria s.7) + Alien Registration Certificate EUR 70 per person. Secure annual income from abroad required (criteria s.2.2): main applicant at least EUR 50,000/year, + EUR 15,000 for a spouse, + EUR 10,000 per minor child (family-of-4 income threshold EUR 85,000/year); for Category A the income must derive from abroad and be proven by tax returns.
routes.family_total_basis: 500 application + 4 x 70 ARC; investment and income requirements are separate
routes.processing_time: Approximately 2 months' examination for a complete application (criteria s.8, read verbatim on the official gov.cy page, 2026-11-14).
routes.residence_requirement: Permit is permanent (card renewed every 10 years) but lapses if the holder does not take up residence within 1 year of approval, or is absent from Cyprus for 2 consecutive years (gov.cy, read verbatim) - in practice at least one entry every 2 years. Post-grant compliance per the gov.cy page's clarifications, which supersede the criteria's s.10 as printed: annual proof of maintaining the investment and of health insurance; police-clearance certificates every 3 years; annual income proof is NOT required (abolished by the clarifications).
routes.time_to_pr: The permit is itself permanent residence
routes.time_to_citizenship: Civil Registry Law 141(I)/2002, art. 111B(1) (as amended 2023, in force 19-12-2023), per the official M127 application page: (a) 12 months' continuous legal residence immediately before applying (absences totalling up to 90 days do not interrupt it); and (b) cumulative legal residence of at least 7 years during the 10 years preceding that final 12-month period. Plus Greek language B1, a civics/history/culture examination pass of at least 60%, clean record, aged 18+. Fees: EUR 500 application + 2 x EUR 8.54 stamps, plus EUR 500 on issuance of the certificate. (The '2,555 days' figure in secondary sources is arithmetic, not official wording.)
routes.dual_citizenship: Allowed in structure: no provision requires renouncing a previous nationality to naturalise, and none removes Cypriot nationality for acquiring another - art. 112 provides a voluntary renunciation channel that presupposes dual holding. Caveat: the proviso to art. 111(1) allows the Council of Ministers to require renunciation for specified cases or categories; no published instance was found. Phrase as 'the law does not require renunciation', not as an unqualified guarantee.

routes.programme: Guest Investor Visa and Residence Permit (Vendégbefektető, Act XC of 2023)
routes.status_note: Fund and donation routes open since 2024-07-01. The legislated EUR 500,000 direct real-estate route was abolished before it ever operated: removed by Act LXXXIV of 2024 (s.135(2) replacing Act XC s.16(3)), gazetted 2024-12-20, effective 2024-12-30 (Act s.41(1)). It would only ever have covered purchases after 2025-01-01, so no property purchase ever qualified.
routes.legal_basis: Act XC of 2023 on the general rules of entry and stay of third-country nationals; administered by the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (OIF)

options.name: Real-estate fund units (National Bank-registered fund)
options.notes: Fund with >= 40% of net assets in Hungarian residential real estate; manager on the official qualifying list; units held at least 5 years in a frozen securities sub-account

options.name: Donation to a public-trust higher-education institution
options.notes: Non-refundable; education/science/art purposes

routes.gov_fees: Guest investor visa 110 (OIF fee page); residence permit via Enter Hungary HUF 26,000 (in person HUF 39,000); extension HUF 26,000. Family-reunification permit fees for dependants are not itemised for this category on the fee page read.
routes.family_total_basis: Visa fee would be 4 x 110 = 440 plus each member's residence-permit fee; dependant fee category not officially itemised — no family total settled
routes.processing_time: 21 days for the guest-investor residence permit (OIF category factsheet s.6), excluding the period between application and submission of proof that the investment was completed - the clock stops for that interval (Act XC of 2023 s.173(1) and s.173(3)(j), the latter added by Act LXXXIV of 2024 s.142). The investor undertakes to complete the investment within 3 months of entry.
routes.residence_requirement: Guest investor visa max 6 months; residence permit max 10 years, extendable once for 10 years. OIF FAQ verbatim: 'there is no rule regarding the minimum length of stay in Hungary for holders of such a permit', and renewal does not test 90 days in the prior 180. Apply for the permit within 30 days of first entry; complete (or prove) the investment within 3 months of entry.
routes.time_to_pr: National Residence Card (permanent residence) after at least 3 years' legal, uninterrupted residence under the general rules (OIF factsheet; absences per Act XC s.84(1): a single absence under 4 months and no more than 270 days in total over the 3 years). The OIF publishes nothing category-specific, but Act XC s.83(5)'s list of categories excluded from this route (guest self-employment, seasonal and employment purposes, guest workers, study, White Card, etc.) does not include the guest investor, and s.84(3)'s non-counting rules likewise omit it - guest-investor residence therefore counts.
routes.time_to_citizenship: 8 years' continuous residence (Act LV of 1993 s.4(1)(a)); preferential 3- and 5-year tiers exist for defined cases (e.g. spouses of Hungarian citizens, former citizens).
routes.dual_citizenship: Allowed: Act LV of 1993 s.2(2) - a Hungarian citizen who also holds another nationality is treated as a Hungarian citizen for the purposes of Hungarian law; renunciation (s.8(1)(a)) presupposes holding a foreign nationality. No renunciation is required to naturalise.
documents: Investment completion or commitment declaration with source-of-funds proof
Fund-unit and frozen-account certificates for the fund route

routes.programme: Investor visa and residence (Ley 14/2013 Arts. 63-67) — CLOSED
routes.status_note: Abolished by Ley Orgánica 1/2025, de 2 de enero (BOE-A-2025-76, published 2025-01-03). Final provision 21 reads (read verbatim): 'Se dejan sin contenido los artículos 63, 64, 65, 66 y 67' — the entire investor chapter of Ley 14/2013 was emptied, all channels (real estate, funds, deposits, bonds, business projects) with no exceptions. The law took effect three months after publication: no new investor applications from 2025-04-03. Transitional rules: applications filed before the effective date are decided under the rules at filing; permits already granted remain valid for their term and renewals are processed under the rules of initial grant (the UGE's June 2025 reading extends this to all investor categories; that extension is administrative interpretation, not BOE text). No replacement investment-residence law had been gazetted as of 2026-11. Retained in v1 as the standing 'stale information' specimen: any source still selling a Spanish golden visa is out of date.
